question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{y\to 3}\frac{{y}^{3}-9y}{{y}^{2}-5y+6} & =\frac{{3}^{3}-9(3)}{{3}^{2}-5(3)+6}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{3}-9y}{{y}^{2}-5y+6} & =\frac{y({y}^{2}-9)}{(y-2)(y-3)} \\  & =\frac{y(y-3)(y+3)}{(y-2)(y-3)} \\  & =\frac{y(y+3)}{(y-2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{y\to 3}\frac{{y}^{3}-9y}{{y}^{2}-5y+6} & ={lim}_{y\to 3}\frac{y(y+3)}{y-2} \\  & =\frac{3(3+3)}{3-2} \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
